name: Strawberry Gazpacho
description: Pickled red onion, strawberries, goat cheese, basil oil
tableside: A chilled summer soup built on strawberries rather than the usual all-tomato base. It comes out cold, so say that when you drop it, because guests who hear soup expect hot. The goat cheese and basil oil are what keep it savoury rather than reading like a dessert.

dairy.note: Goat cheese can be left off.

gluten.note: Traditional gazpacho is thickened with bread. Confirm the base with the kitchen before clearing a celiac guest.

key_terms.definition: A cold raw-vegetable soup from Andalusia in southern Spain, traditionally thickened with stale bread and built on tomato. Eaten through the summer as a way of using ripe produce without cooking. This version leads with strawberry instead.
Basil blanched briefly in boiling water, shocked cold, then blended with oil and strained. The blanching sets the chlorophyll so the oil stays bright green rather than browning within the hour.

chef_notes: Served cold. Guests who expect a hot soup should be told before it lands. Confirm whether the base is bread-thickened before clearing anyone for gluten.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Hillinger Secco, Burgenland NV
wine_pairings_btg.note: Secco's light bubble and low sweetness lifts the strawberry without pushing the soup toward dessert.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Tement Zweigelt Rosé, Niederösterreich
wine_pairings_btg.note: Zweigelt rosé picks up the strawberry directly and its acidity resets the palate against the goat cheese.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Arianna Occhipinti SP68 White, Sicily 2024
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Skin contact gives it enough grip to stand up to pickled onion, and the aromatics run alongside the basil oil.

name: Baby Kale Salad
description: Plumcot, goat cheese, pepita, pumpkin seed oil
tableside: Baby kale, so it's tender rather than the tough curly kind. Plumcot is a plum and apricot cross, and it carries the sweetness here.

dairy.note: Goat cheese can be left off.

nuts.note: Pepitas are pumpkin seeds, not tree nuts. Flag for guests who avoid seeds.

gluten.note: No gluten in the components.

key_terms.definition: A cross between a plum and an apricot, roughly half of each. Sweeter and softer than a plum, with apricot aromatics.
A hulled pumpkin seed. Toasted for crunch. A seed, not a tree nut, though seed-avoidant guests should still be told.
Dark green, thick, and strongly nutty. A Styrian specialty in Austria, where it is a regional staple rather than a garnish.

chef_notes: Pepitas and pumpkin seed oil are both seeds. They do not trigger tree nut protocols, but say so plainly rather than just answering no to a nut question.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner's white pepper and green edge runs with the kale, and the acidity handles the goat cheese.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Paris-Simoneau Sauvignon Blanc, Val de Loire
wine_pairings_btg.note: Loire Sauvignon keeps the plumcot sweetness in check and echoes the green herbal side of the salad.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Tement Morillon 'Muschelkalk,' Styria 2019
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Styrian Chardonnay from the same region as the pumpkin seed oil, with the weight to carry it.

name: Burgundy Escargot
description: Chipotle Buffalo Trace butter, toast points, chives
tableside: Classic Burgundy snails, but the butter is built with chipotle and Buffalo Trace instead of the usual garlic and parsley. The toast points are for mopping, and most of the pleasure is in the butter rather than the snails themselves. Worth saying so to a hesitant guest.

shellfish.note: Escargot are land snails, which are molluscs. They are not crustacean shellfish, but a guest avoiding molluscs should avoid this dish. Ask which they react to.

dairy.note: Built on a compound butter. Central to the dish.

gluten.note: From the toast points. Can be served without bread or with a gluten free substitute.

key_terms.definition: Land snails, a Burgundian classic going back centuries. Cooked in seasoned butter and served either in the shell or in a dish with wells. Texture is closer to a mushroom than to shellfish, which is usually the reassurance a nervous guest needs.
A jalapeño ripened to red and then smoke dried, usually over several days. It brings smoke and a slow moderate heat rather than the sharp front-of-mouth burn of a fresh chili.
Bread sliced thin, crusts trimmed, toasted and cut into triangles. Here they are structural rather than decorative, since they are the only way to get the butter off the plate.

chef_notes: The shellfish question is worth handling carefully. Snails are molluscs but not crustaceans, and guests use the word shellfish for both. Ask what specifically they react to rather than answering yes or no.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner's pepper meets the chipotle head on and the acidity cuts a butter this rich.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Maison de la Villette Pinot Noir, Loire Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Light Loire Pinot is the Burgundian answer, and it has enough fruit to sit against the smoke.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: The Vice Pinot Noir, Torie's Vineyard, Los Carneros 2024
wine_pairings_bottle.note: More fruit weight than the glass pour, which absorbs the chipotle heat instead of fighting it.

name: Shrimp and Grits
description: Whiskey cream, spinach, caramelized onion, aleppo chili crisp
tableside: Whiskey goes into the cream sauce. Aleppo chili crisp on top brings a mild, fruity heat rather than a sharp one.

dairy.note: Cream sauce and the grits themselves.

gluten.note: Chili crisp often contains wheat and the cream may be flour thickened. Confirm both with the kitchen.

soy.note: Chili crisp commonly contains soy. Confirm the brand or preparation.

key_terms.definition: Coarsely ground dried corn, simmered until creamy. A Southern staple, distinct from polenta mainly by the corn variety and grind.
A Syrian chili, sun dried and coarsely crushed. Fruity and raisin-like with slow moderate heat rather than a sharp front.
A condiment of fried chili and aromatics suspended in oil. Texture as much as heat.

chef_notes: Two allergens hide in the chili crisp: wheat and soy are both common in commercial versions. Do not clear a celiac or soy allergy on this dish without checking.

wine_pairings_btg.name: The Vice Chardonnay, Napa Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Napa Chardonnay has the weight for the cream and enough acid to keep the grits from sitting heavy.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Tement Zweigelt Rosé, Niederösterreich
wine_pairings_btg.note: Zweigelt rosé handles the aleppo heat better than a white and stays clean against the shrimp.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: The Calling Chardonnay, Sonoma Coast 2019
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Oak and body meet the whiskey cream at the bottle level without burying the shrimp.

name: Cajun Corn Ribs
description: Cilantro, lime, parmesan cream dipping sauce
tableside: Corn on the cob cut lengthwise into strips, which curl as they cook and end up looking like ribs. Eaten with your hands, so warn a table that might not expect that. The parmesan cream comes on the side, which makes the dairy easy to hold.

shellfish.note: No shellfish in the corn. Confirm the Cajun blend, as some contain crustacean-derived seasoning.

dairy.note: The parmesan cream is a dipping sauce and can be held or served on the side.

gluten.note: Cajun spice blends sometimes contain wheat, and fryer sharing is a factor. Confirm before clearing a celiac guest.

eggs.note: Confirm whether the cream sauce has a mayonnaise or emulsified base.

soy.note: No soy expected. Confirm frying oil if a guest is strict.

vegetarian.note: No meat or fish, though parmesan is not always vegetarian rennet. Confirm if it matters to the guest.

key_terms.definition: Corn on the cob quartered lengthwise down the cob. Heat makes the kernels contract faster than the cob, so the strip curls into a rib shape. Entirely a texture play, and it has to be eaten by hand.

A Louisiana blend built on paprika, cayenne, garlic, onion, black pepper and dried herbs. Warm and savoury more than sharply hot, and distinct from Creole seasoning, which leans more heavily on herbs.

chef_notes: Eaten by hand. Warn tables who might not expect that. The dipping sauce comes on the side, which makes the dairy easy to hold.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Michael-Eppan Pinot Grigio, Alto Adige
wine_pairings_btg.note: Pinot Grigio's clean citrus keeps up with the lime and does not compete with the Cajun spice.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Hillinger Secco, Burgenland NV
wine_pairings_btg.note: Bubbles cut the parmesan cream and reset between bites of a spiced, hand-eaten dish.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Elk Cove Pinot Blanc, Willamette Valley 2024
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Round enough for the cream sauce, dry enough to stay out of the way of the spice.

name: Buffalo Chicken Dip
description: Old Bay prawn chips, panko, chives
tableside: A hot dip served with prawn chips instead of celery, and those chips are genuinely shrimp based rather than shrimp flavoured. That matters for allergy tables and is worth raising before anyone digs in. Meant for sharing across a table.

shellfish.note: The prawn chips are shrimp based. The dip itself is not, so ask the kitchen whether an alternative vehicle is possible.

dairy.note: Cream cheese and cheese base. Central to the dish.

gluten.note: Panko is wheat breadcrumb.

eggs.note: Ranch or mayonnaise components may contain egg. Confirm the base.

soy.note: Buffalo sauce and prawn chips may contain soy. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: A puffed cracker made from ground shrimp and tapioca starch, common across Southeast Asia. It contains real shellfish protein, so it is not safe for a shellfish allergy no matter how little shrimp it tastes of.
A Chesapeake seasoning blend heavy on celery salt, paprika and black pepper, created in Baltimore in the 1940s. Regional shorthand for Maryland crab country and used on almost everything here.
Japanese breadcrumb made from crustless bread baked without crust browning. The flakes are larger and airier than standard crumb, so it absorbs less oil and stays crisp considerably longer.

chef_notes: The shellfish is in the chips, not the dip. That distinction is worth raising with an allergy table rather than refusing the dish outright, but check with the kitchen before promising a substitute.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Hillinger Secco, Burgenland NV
wine_pairings_btg.note: Bubbles and chill against a hot, rich, salty dip.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Michael-Eppan Pinot Grigio, Alto Adige
wine_pairings_btg.note: Pinot Grigio is neutral enough not to fight the buffalo heat and cold enough to reset.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Anton Bauer Riesling, Feuersbrunn 2021
wine_pairings_bottle.note: A trace of Riesling sweetness takes the edge off buffalo heat in a way a dry white cannot.

name: Baked Brie
description: Cherry jam, candied pecans
tableside: Baked until it runs. Cherry jam and candied pecans on top. Meant for sharing.

dairy.note: Brie is the dish.

nuts.note: Pecans are a garnish and can be left off.

gluten.note: Served with bread or crostini. Confirm whether a gluten free vehicle is available.

vegetarian.note: Confirm rennet with the kitchen if the guest is strict.

key_terms.definition: A soft cow's milk cheese from northern France with a bloomy rind. Warming it makes the paste run.
Pecans cooked in sugar until glazed. The coating adds crunch and keeps them from softening in the warm cheese.

chef_notes: Pecans come off easily. The bread is the harder problem for a celiac guest, so ask the kitchen about the vehicle before promising anything.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Hillinger Secco, Burgenland NV
wine_pairings_btg.note: Bubbles against melted cheese, and the Secco has enough fruit to meet the cherry jam.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Maison de la Villette Pinot Noir, Loire Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Loire Pinot picks up the cherry directly and stays light enough not to bury the brie.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Hillinger 'Hillside,' Leithaberg 2022
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Austrian red blend with red fruit that runs straight at the cherry jam and soft enough tannin for a soft cheese.

name: BBQ Bone Marrow
description: Apricot jam, mint gremolata, ciabatta
tableside: Roasted marrow bones, scooped and spread on the ciabatta. Rich, so it works better shared than solo.

dairy.note: Confirm whether butter is used in roasting or in the gremolata.

nuts.note: Gremolata is classically parsley, garlic, and lemon zest with no nuts, but confirm this version.

gluten.note: From the ciabatta. Can be served with a gluten free substitute or without bread.

soy.note: BBQ glazes frequently contain soy. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: The fatty tissue inside beef leg bones. Roasted until it loosens, then spread. Texture closer to butter than to meat.
An Italian condiment of chopped parsley, garlic, and lemon zest. Cuts richness. Mint here in place of or alongside the parsley.

chef_notes: Very rich. Steer solo diners toward sharing it or pair it with something acidic. Marrow that sits too long stiffens up, so it should go out hot.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steindorfer Blaufränkisch, Burgenland
wine_pairings_btg.note: Blaufränkisch brings peppery acidity that cuts marrow fat without adding weight.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Ontañon Tempranillo/Garnacha, Crianza, Rioja
wine_pairings_btg.note: Rioja's savory edge and firm structure keep the richness moving.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Glatzer Blaufränkisch, Göttlesbrunn DAC 2020
wine_pairings_bottle.note: More concentrated than the glass pour, with the tannin structure to reset the palate against pure fat.

wine_pairings_whisky.name: Weller Antique 107
wine_pairings_whisky.note: Wheated bourbon at 107 proof. The proof cuts marrow fat and the wheat keeps it from turning harsh against the apricot.

name: Salmon Belly
description: Bourbon cured and baked, apple vin., radish, arugula, mustard seed gastrique
tableside: The belly is the fattiest cut of the salmon. Cured in bourbon, then baked, so it is served warm rather than as a cold cure.

shellfish.note: Salmon is finfish, not shellfish. Guests avoiding all seafood should still avoid it.

dairy.note: No dairy expected. Confirm if butter is used in baking.

gluten.note: Confirm the bourbon cure and gastrique components with the kitchen.

soy.note: No soy expected. Confirm the gastrique.

key_terms.definition: The fattiest part of the fish, cut from underneath. Higher fat than the loin, so it stays moist and reads richer.
A sweet and sour sauce built by cooking sugar to caramel and deglazing with vinegar. Here it carries mustard seed.
Drawing moisture out with salt and sugar, firming texture and concentrating flavor. Bourbon here adds aromatics on top of that.

chef_notes: Cured then baked, so it arrives warm. Guests who hear cured may expect cold gravlax. Say it plainly when you drop it.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner's acidity and pepper cut the belly fat and pick up the mustard seed.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Tement Zweigelt Rosé, Niederösterreich
wine_pairings_btg.note: Zweigelt rosé has the weight for an oily fish and enough acid for the vinegar.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Hanna Glatzer Weiss Traminer, Carnuntum 2021
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Skin contact texture matches the fat on the belly, and the aromatics ride with the mustard seed.

name: Loaded Pierogies
description: Cheddar, bacon crumble, dill crema, crispy shallots
tableside: Potato pierogi finished like a loaded baked potato. Filling and easy to share.

dairy.note: Cheddar and crema. Central to the dish.

gluten.note: Pierogi dough is wheat.

eggs.note: Pierogi dough commonly contains egg. Confirm this recipe.

soy.note: Confirm the frying oil and bacon cure.

vegetarian.note: Bacon can be left off. Confirm the dough and any stock used.

vegan.note: Dough, cheese, and crema all contain animal product.

key_terms.definition: A filled dumpling from Poland and across Central Europe. Boiled, then usually pan fried. Potato and cheese is the standard filling.
A cultured cream, thinner and less sour than sour cream, so it pours rather than sits.

chef_notes: Substantial for an appetizer. Worth flagging to a table ordering several starters plus mains.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner is the regional answer to a Central European dumpling and its acidity handles cheddar and bacon fat.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steindorfer Blaufränkisch, Burgenland
wine_pairings_btg.note: Blaufränkisch has the acidity for the fat without tannin that would fight the potato.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Jurtschitsch Grüner Veltliner Terrassen 2023
wine_pairings_bottle.note: More concentration than the glass pour while staying in the same regional register as the dish.

name: Focaccia
description: Strawberry basil balsamic & olive oil
tableside: House focaccia with a strawberry basil balsamic and olive oil for dipping. This replaced the Parker House rolls. There is no gluten free version of it, so a celiac guest should be pointed at the skillet cornbread instead.

dairy.note: Focaccia is typically made with olive oil rather than butter. Confirm.

gluten.note: Wheat bread. Cannot be modified.

eggs.note: Standard focaccia contains no egg. Confirm.

vegan.note: Likely vegan, but confirm no dairy or honey in the dough or balsamic.

key_terms.definition: A flat oven-baked Italian bread, dimpled with the fingertips and generous with olive oil. Softer and considerably thicker than pizza dough, and the dimples exist to hold oil and salt rather than for looks.
Aged grape must vinegar from Modena, cooked down and aged in wood. Sweet and syrupy rather than sharp, which is why it works alongside fruit instead of fighting it.

chef_notes: Replaced the Parker House rolls. No gluten free version of this one, so direct celiac guests to the skillet cornbread instead.

name: GF Skillet Cornbread
description: Watermelon jam
tableside: Gluten free cornbread baked in a skillet, served with watermelon jam. This is the gluten free bread option.

dairy.note: Cornbread is usually made with butter or buttermilk. Confirm before clearing a dairy allergy.

gluten.note: Made gluten free. Confirm skillet and prep surface separation for a celiac guest.

vegan.note: Likely contains dairy and egg. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: Cornbread baked in a preheated cast iron pan, which sets a crust on the bottom and edges.
Watermelon cooked down with sugar and pectin. Milder and more floral than a berry jam.

chef_notes: This is the gluten free bread option, but it is only reliably gluten free, not dairy or egg free. Do not assume gluten free means allergen free.

name: Butcher Salad
description: Creme fraiche vin., tomato, cucumber, bacon, spit roasted meat
tableside: Whatever is on the rotisserie that night goes on this salad. Ask the kitchen what the meat is before you promise anything.

dairy.note: Creme fraiche vinaigrette can be served on the side or swapped.

gluten.note: Depends on the rotisserie meat's rub and any jus. Confirm nightly.

eggs.note: No eggs expected in the vinaigrette. Confirm.

soy.note: Depends on the night's meat preparation.

key_terms.definition: A cultured cream, richer and less sour than sour cream, with enough fat that it will not split in a vinaigrette.
Cooked on a rotating rotisserie. The turning bastes the meat in its own fat as it renders.

chef_notes: The meat changes with the rotisserie. Typically shredded chicken and steak, but confirm each evening rather than assuming. Allergen answers depend on what is on the spit that night.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Tement Zweigelt Rosé, Niederösterreich
wine_pairings_btg.note: Zweigelt rosé handles both the smoke on the meat and the acidity of the vinaigrette.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steindorfer Blaufränkisch, Burgenland
wine_pairings_btg.note: Blaufränkisch has the pepper for the rotisserie char without tannin that would flatten a salad.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Glatzer Zweigelt 'Dornenvogel,' Göttlesbrunn DAC 2021
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Enough fruit for the smoke, light enough tannin to sit against raw tomato and cucumber.

name: Joyce Farm Chicken
description: Roasted root vegetables, patty pan squash, lemon herb tahini
tableside: Half or whole. Always confirm which one the guest wants, since the whole bird is a serious amount of food.

dairy.note: Confirm whether butter is used on the vegetables.

nuts.note: Tahini is sesame, a seed rather than a tree nut. Tell sesame-avoidant guests directly.

gluten.note: Confirm the rub and any jus.

soy.note: No soy expected. Confirm the tahini blend.

key_terms.definition: A North Carolina producer raising slower-growing heritage birds. More developed flavor and firmer texture than commodity chicken.
A small round summer squash with scalloped edges. Mild, tender, and quick cooking.
Ground sesame seed paste. Sesame is a top-nine allergen in the United States and is not a tree nut.

chef_notes: Half is $32, whole is $60. Always confirm before firing. Sesame is a declarable allergen in its own right, so name it rather than clearing the dish as nut free and stopping there.

wine_pairings_btg.name: The Vice Chardonnay, Napa Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Napa Chardonnay has the body for rotisserie chicken and enough weight for the tahini.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner's citrus and pepper cut the tahini richness and keep the root vegetables from reading heavy.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Prieler Chardonnay, Schützen Ried Sinner, Leithaberg 2024
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Austrian Chardonnay with more mineral drive than Napa, which keeps the sesame from coating the palate.

name: Whole Roasted Fish
description: Carrot, ginger, red pepper, peanut & coconut curry, peanut, smoked cashews
tableside: A whole fish, served on the bone. The curry is peanut and coconut based, so this is a hard no for anyone with a peanut or tree nut allergy.

shellfish.note: The fish is finfish, but curries of this style often contain fish sauce or shrimp paste. Confirm with the kitchen.

dairy.note: Coconut milk, not dairy cream.

nuts.note: Smoked cashews and coconut. Cannot be modified, the curry is nut based.

peanuts.note: Peanuts are in the curry base and as a garnish. Cannot be modified.

gluten.note: Confirm the curry paste and any finishing sauce.

soy.note: Curry pastes of this style frequently contain soy. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: Cooked on the bone with the head on. The bone keeps it moist and adds flavor. Ask whether the guest wants it filleted tableside.
A curry built on ground peanut and coconut milk. The peanut is structural, not a garnish.
Classified as a tree nut by the FDA for labeling, though botanically a drupe. Most tree nut allergic guests tolerate it, but never assume on their behalf.

chef_notes: The single highest-risk dish on the menu for nut allergies. Peanut is in the curry base and cannot be removed. Confirm the species with the kitchen each evening, as this has historically been branzino but the preparation has changed.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Michael-Eppan Pinot Grigio, Alto Adige
wine_pairings_btg.note: Pinot Grigio stays out of the way of a peanut curry and the chill resets against the coconut fat.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Tement Zweigelt Rosé, Niederösterreich
wine_pairings_btg.note: Zweigelt rosé has the fruit to meet the ginger and red pepper without adding tannin.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Mosbach Gewürztraminer, Alsace NV
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Aromatic and slightly off dry, which is the classic move against ginger and chili heat in a coconut base.

name: Rohan Duck Breast
description: Aleppo chili crisp, duck fat potatoes
tableside: Tuesday's rotisserie feature. Rohan is a specific duck breed, leaner and less gamey than a Pekin. Limited availability, so check the count before you sell it.

dairy.note: Confirm whether butter is used on the potatoes.

gluten.note: Chili crisp often contains wheat. Confirm before clearing a celiac guest.

soy.note: Chili crisp commonly contains soy. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: A crossbreed developed in New York, leaner than Pekin and milder than Moulard. Takes well to rendering.
Potatoes roasted in rendered duck fat, which crisps the exterior more aggressively than oil.
A Syrian chili, sun dried and crushed. Fruity, moderate, slow heat rather than a sharp front.

chef_notes: This replaced the Ibérico rack of pork on Tuesdays. Limited availability, so confirm the count with the kitchen before selling it hard. All rotisserie features come with duck fat potatoes, which means the sides are not vegetarian either.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Maison de la Villette Pinot Noir, Loire Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Loire Pinot is the standard against duck, light enough not to bury a lean breast.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steindorfer Blaufränkisch, Burgenland
wine_pairings_btg.note: Blaufränkisch has pepper that meets the aleppo directly and acidity for the duck fat.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Joseph Drouhin Roserock Pinot Noir, Eola-Amity Hills 2021
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Oregon Pinot with more density than the glass pour and the earth to sit under the chili crisp.

name: Whole Rack of Lamb
description: Basil & pine nut-arugula pesto, duck fat potatoes
tableside: Wednesday's rotisserie feature. Whole rack, so it is a substantial portion. The pesto contains pine nuts.

dairy.note: Pesto usually contains parmesan. Confirm this version.

nuts.note: Pine nuts in the pesto. Ask whether the kitchen can serve the lamb without it.

gluten.note: Confirm the rub and jus.

key_terms.definition: The rib section, cooked whole and carved between the bones. Cooked to a set temperature rather than to order when it comes off the rotisserie.
The seed of certain pine species. Classified and treated as a tree nut for allergy purposes.
Basil, garlic, nuts, cheese, and oil, blended. Arugula here adds a peppery edge basil alone would not have.

chef_notes: Pine nuts are treated as tree nuts. The pesto is where they are, so ask the kitchen whether the lamb can go out without it rather than clearing or refusing the dish outright.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steindorfer Blaufränkisch, Burgenland
wine_pairings_btg.note: Blaufränkisch pepper and acid meet the arugula in the pesto and cut lamb fat.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Black Stallion Cabernet Sauvignon, North Coast
wine_pairings_btg.note: Cabernet tannin handles lamb richness, and the herbal edge in the wine runs with the basil.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Heidi Schröck Blaufränkisch, Ried Kulm 2023
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Burgenland Blaufränkisch with more structure than the glass pour, still peppery enough to track the pesto.

wine_pairings_whisky.name: Russell's Reserve 13 Year
wine_pairings_whisky.note: Barrel proof bourbon with oak depth that meets roasted lamb fat, and enough sweetness to sit against a herbal pesto.

name: Tomahawk Ribeye
description: Salsa verde, duck fat potatoes
tableside: Thursday's rotisserie feature. Long bone in ribeye. Large enough to share, and worth saying so.

shellfish.note: Some salsa verde recipes contain anchovy. Confirm this version.

dairy.note: Confirm butter on the potatoes or in basting.

nuts.note: No tree nuts expected. Confirm the salsa verde.

gluten.note: Italian style salsa verde sometimes uses bread as a thickener. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: A ribeye cut with the entire rib bone left long and frenched. The bone is presentation as much as flavor.
A green herb sauce. The Italian version is parsley, capers, anchovy, and vinegar; the Mexican version is tomatillo based. Confirm which one this is, since the anchovy matters for allergies.

chef_notes: Large format cut, easily shared. Confirm whether the salsa verde is the Italian anchovy version or tomatillo based, because that changes the answer for both fish allergies and vegetarian-adjacent questions.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Black Stallion Cabernet Sauvignon, North Coast
wine_pairings_btg.note: Cabernet tannin against ribeye fat is the most direct pairing on the menu.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Ontañon Tempranillo/Garnacha, Crianza, Rioja
wine_pairings_btg.note: Rioja's savory oak and acidity handle the char and cut through the fat.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Acumen 'Mountainside' Cabernet, Atlas Peak, Napa Valley
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Mountain fruit Cabernet with firm tannin built for a fatty cut, available by the glass through Coravin.

wine_pairings_whisky.name: Stagg Batch 25D
wine_pairings_whisky.note: Barrel proof at 63.2 percent. The proof stands up to a heavily charred fatty cut instead of disappearing under it.

name: Prime Rib
description: Horseradish cream, duck fat potatoes
tableside: Friday and Saturday. Ten ounce or sixteen ounce, always confirm which. Comes with horseradish cream on the side.

dairy.note: Horseradish cream is served alongside and can be held.

gluten.note: Confirm the jus and rub with the kitchen.

eggs.note: No eggs expected. Confirm the horseradish cream base.

key_terms.definition: A standing rib roast cooked slowly whole, then carved. Different from a ribeye steak, which is cut from the same primal but seared individually.
Grated horseradish root folded into cream. The heat is volatile and fades with time and heat, which is why it goes out cold and fresh.

chef_notes: Ten ounce is $45, sixteen ounce is $60. Always confirm the size before firing. Sells out on busy Fridays and Saturdays, so check availability with the kitchen through service.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Black Stallion Cabernet Sauvignon, North Coast
wine_pairings_btg.note: Cabernet is the default against prime rib, with tannin for the fat and fruit for the crust.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Ontañon Tempranillo/Garnacha, Crianza, Rioja
wine_pairings_btg.note: Rioja's savory character and acidity keep a heavy cut from sitting flat.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Joseph Carr 'Revelist' Cabernet, Napa Valley 2019
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Napa Cabernet with the concentration to meet a large format roast at the bottle level.

wine_pairings_whisky.name: Eagle Rare 10 Year
wine_pairings_whisky.note: Ten year bourbon with oak and caramel depth that runs alongside the roasted crust without overwhelming the beef.

name: Pan Seared Mahi-Mahi
description: Cauliflower puree, braised cauliflower, pickled cauliflower
tableside: Cauliflower three ways: pureed, braised, and pickled, so the guest gets three textures of the same vegetable across the plate. Mahi is a firm meaty white fish rather than a delicate one, and it takes a hard sear well. It also overcooks fast.

dairy.note: Cauliflower puree is commonly finished with cream or butter. Confirm.

gluten.note: No gluten expected in the components. Confirm the braising liquid.

key_terms.definition: Also called dorado or dolphinfish, and unrelated to dolphins, which is worth clarifying if a guest hesitates. Firm, lean and mild, which is why it holds a hard sear where a softer fish would fall apart.
Presenting one ingredient in several preparations on the same plate so the guest reads the differences in texture and intensity side by side. A way of making a humble vegetable the point of the dish.

chef_notes: Replaced the salmon in this slot. Mahi is lean, so it overcooks fast. Confirm the puree base before clearing a dairy allergy.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Paris-Simoneau Sauvignon Blanc, Val de Loire
wine_pairings_btg.note: Loire Sauvignon's acidity meets the pickled cauliflower and keeps a lean fish bright.

wine_pairings_btg.name: The Vice Chardonnay, Napa Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Chardonnay's weight matches the cauliflower puree if the guest wants something rounder.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Botanica Chenin Blanc 'Mary Delany,' Citrusdal
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Chenin has the texture for the puree and the acid for the pickle, available by the glass through Coravin.

name: Pan Seared U12 Scallops
description: Summer succotash, okra, heirloom tomato, lima bean, pickled garlic, achiote jus
tableside: Six ounces of U12 scallops seared to order. U12 means under twelve scallops per pound, so each one is large.

shellfish.note: Scallops are shellfish. Cannot be modified.

dairy.note: Succotash is frequently finished with butter. Confirm.

gluten.note: No gluten expected. Confirm the jus.

key_terms.definition: Under twelve scallops per pound. Larger scallops sear better because the crust sets before the center overcooks. Each guest gets six ounces regardless of count.
A dish of corn and beans, originally from the Narragansett. Summer versions add whatever else is at peak.
Annatto seed, which gives a deep red-orange color and a mild earthy, peppery flavor. Used widely in Latin American and Filipino cooking.

chef_notes: Six ounces per guest regardless of individual scallop count. Scallops cannot be modified out of the dish.

wine_pairings_btg.name: The Vice Chardonnay, Napa Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Chardonnay's weight matches a seared scallop and the succotash without flattening the achiote.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Paris-Simoneau Sauvignon Blanc, Val de Loire
wine_pairings_btg.note: Sauvignon's acidity lifts the tomato and pickled garlic and keeps the scallop sweetness defined.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Clementine Carter Roussanne, Santa Barbara County
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Roussanne has the body for seared scallops and enough texture for the succotash, poured by the glass through Coravin.

name: Summer Seafood Stew
description: PEI mussels, shrimp, mkt fish, tomato, corn, toasted ciabatta
tableside: Mussels, shrimp, and whatever the market fish is that day, in a tomato and corn broth. Confirm the fish with the kitchen.

shellfish.note: Mussels and shrimp. Cannot be modified.

dairy.note: Confirm whether the broth is finished with butter or cream.

gluten.note: From the ciabatta. Can be served without bread or with a substitute. Confirm the broth is not flour thickened.

key_terms.definition: Prince Edward Island mussels, rope cultivated in cold Canadian water. Cleaner and less gritty than wild harvested.
Whatever the kitchen has that day. Always confirm before quoting it to a guest.
The Belgian stew this dish evolved from. That name is internal only and does not appear on the printed menu.

chef_notes: This was the Belgian Seafood Stew and is now built on a summer tomato and corn base. Confirm the market fish each evening. Two shellfish types in one bowl, neither removable.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Michael-Eppan Pinot Grigio, Alto Adige
wine_pairings_btg.note: Pinot Grigio is clean and cold against a tomato broth without competing with the shellfish.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Tement Zweigelt Rosé, Niederösterreich
wine_pairings_btg.note: Zweigelt rosé is the southern French move on a seafood stew and handles the tomato acidity.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Domaine Berthet-Rayne Côtes du Rhône Blanc 2020
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Rhône white has the body for a brothy stew and enough weight for the corn sweetness.

name: Smoke in Chimneys Seared Rainbow Trout
description: Lollipop kale sprouts, pine nuts, capers, lemon
tableside: Smoke in Chimneys is a trout farm in Newport, Virginia, raising fish in constant cold spring water. This is the most local protein on the menu and the sourcing is worth leading with. Pine nuts are the allergen to watch, and they are a garnish rather than structural.

dairy.note: Preparations like this are commonly finished with butter. Confirm.

nuts.note: Pine nuts are treated as tree nuts. Ask whether they can be left off.

gluten.note: No gluten expected in the components. Confirm any dredge on the fish.

key_terms.definition: A trout farm in Newport, Virginia, named for the mountain above it. The fish grow in spring water held at a constant cold temperature year round, which produces firmer flesh than pond-raised trout.
A cross between kale and Brussels sprouts, growing as small loose rosettes along a stalk. Milder and sweeter than either parent, and they crisp at the edges rather than going bitter.
The pickled flower bud of the caper bush, which grows wild across the Mediterranean. Salty and floral, and used here for the same reason lemon is: to cut through the fat of an oily fish.

sourcing: Smoke in Chimneys trout farm, Newport, Virginia
chef_notes: The most local protein on the menu and the sourcing story is worth leading with. Pine nuts are the allergen to watch, and they are a garnish rather than structural.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner's citrus and mineral edge is a direct match for trout with lemon and capers.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Paris-Simoneau Sauvignon Blanc, Val de Loire
wine_pairings_btg.note: Sauvignon Blanc's acidity handles the capers and keeps a rich fish clean.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Paradise Springs Petit Manseng, Clifton 2023
wine_pairings_bottle.note: A Virginia white with a Virginia fish, and Petit Manseng's acidity is built for capers and lemon.

name: 8oz Snake River Farms Wagyu Flat Iron Steak
description: Mixed bean almondine, purple haze goat cheese, rosemary garlic butter
tableside: American Wagyu from Snake River Farms, and flat iron is a well marbled shoulder cut that eats far more tender than its price suggests. Cooked to order, so always take a temperature. Almondine means almonds, which is the allergen headline here.
ingredients: Snake River Farms Wagyu flat iron

dairy.note: Goat cheese and the compound butter. Ask the kitchen whether both can be held.

nuts.note: Almondine means almonds. Ask whether the beans can go out without them.

gluten.note: No gluten expected. Confirm any rub.

key_terms.definition: An Idaho producer crossing Japanese Wagyu genetics with American Black Angus. The result carries far more intramuscular marbling than commodity beef without reaching the extreme richness of full Japanese A5.
Cut from the shoulder, and second only to the tenderloin in tenderness once the central line of sinew is removed. Well marbled and considerably beefier in flavour than a filet.
A preparation finished with toasted sliced almonds, from the French amandine. The almonds are the definition of the dish rather than a garnish, so the name itself is the allergy warning.
A fresh goat cheese from Cypress Grove in California, flavoured with lavender and fennel pollen. Soft, bright and floral rather than sharp.

sourcing: Snake River Farms American Wagyu, Idaho
chef_notes: Cooked to order, so always take a temperature. Almondine is the allergen headline, and the name itself tells you almonds are there, so do not let it slip past on a nut allergy table.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Black Stallion Cabernet Sauvignon, North Coast
wine_pairings_btg.note: Cabernet tannin against Wagyu marbling, with enough fruit to meet the rosemary butter.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steindorfer Blaufränkisch, Burgenland
wine_pairings_btg.note: Blaufränkisch for a guest who wants acidity rather than tannin against a fatty cut.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Acumen 'Mountainside' Cabernet, Atlas Peak, Napa Valley
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Mountain tannin structured for high marbling, poured by the glass through Coravin.

name: Wienerschnitzel from Pork
description: Dill potato salad, lingonberry jam
tableside: Pounded thin, breaded, and fried. Ours is pork rather than veal, which is the standard Viennese distinction worth naming.

dairy.note: Confirm the frying medium and the potato salad dressing.

gluten.note: Breaded in wheat crumb. Cannot be modified.

eggs.note: Egg is part of the breading standard. Confirm the potato salad dressing as well.

key_terms.definition: Legally in Austria this term means veal. Made with pork it is properly Schnitzel vom Schwein, which is why the menu names the pork explicitly.
A tart red berry from Northern Europe, similar to a cranberry. The sharpness is what cuts the fried breading.
The Austrian breading sequence of flour, egg, then crumb. The crumb layer should puff away from the meat rather than sit tight against it.

chef_notes: The house signature and the most Austrian thing on the menu. Breading means gluten and egg are both structural and neither can be removed.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner Veltliner with schnitzel is the Austrian pairing, and the acidity cuts fried breading.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Michael-Eppan Pinot Grigio, Alto Adige
wine_pairings_btg.note: Pinot Grigio if the guest wants something lighter, clean enough not to fight the lingonberry.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Bründlmayer Ried Berg Vogelsang 1ÖTW, Kamptal 2023
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Single vineyard Grüner with the concentration to make the classic pairing worth trading up for.

name: Roasted Zucchiolo
description: Sheep milk feta, zatar spiced pistachio, preserved lemon, Goldberry Hill honey vin.
tableside: This is the vegetarian main. Zucchiolo sits between a zucchini and a marrow, so it holds up to roasting where a regular zucchini would collapse. Honey in the vinaigrette means it is not vegan as written, which catches people out.

dairy.note: Sheep milk feta can be left off.

nuts.note: Pistachios. Ask whether they can be held.

gluten.note: Some za'atar blends are cut with wheat. Confirm before clearing a celiac guest.

vegetarian.note: No meat or fish. Confirm the feta rennet if the guest is strict.

vegan.note: Contains feta and honey. Ask the kitchen whether both can be replaced.

key_terms.definition: A summer squash between a zucchini and a marrow in size, with denser flesh and fewer seeds. That density is what lets it roast properly instead of going watery.

A Levantine blend of dried thyme or oregano, sumac, toasted sesame and salt. Recipes vary by family and region, and some commercial blends are extended with wheat flour, which is why it needs checking.
Lemons packed in salt for weeks until the rind softens completely. Only the peel is used, and it reads floral and savoury rather than sour, since the salt draws out most of the acidity.
A Virginia honey producer. The honey in the vinaigrette is the reason this dish is vegetarian rather than vegan.

chef_notes: This is the vegetarian main. Guests asking for vegan need the feta and the honey vinaigrette both addressed, so check with the kitchen rather than just pulling the cheese.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Paris-Simoneau Sauvignon Blanc, Val de Loire
wine_pairings_btg.note: Sauvignon's herbal edge runs with the za'atar and the acidity meets the preserved lemon.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Steininger Grüner Veltliner, Ried Loisium, Kamptal
wine_pairings_btg.note: Grüner's pepper and citrus handle the honey sweetness without turning cloying.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Arianna Occhipinti SP68 White, Sicily 2024
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Skin contact texture stands up to roasted squash and the wine's savory edge tracks the za'atar.

name: Spring Chicken Cavatelli
description: Asparagus, English peas, radish, cured egg yolk
tableside: Cavatelli is a small rolled pasta with a hollow that catches sauce. The cured egg yolk is grated over at the pass.

dairy.note: Confirm whether the sauce is finished with butter or cheese.

gluten.note: Cavatelli is wheat pasta. Cannot be modified.

eggs.note: The cured yolk is grated on top and can be held. Confirm whether the pasta dough contains egg.

vegan.note: Contains chicken, wheat pasta, and egg.

key_terms.definition: A small shell-shaped pasta from southern Italy, rolled so it curls. The hollow holds sauce better than a smooth shape.
A yolk buried in salt and sugar until firm enough to grate. Behaves like a hard cheese with a deeper savory note.

chef_notes: The cured yolk is a finishing garnish, so an egg allergy does not necessarily kill the dish. Confirm whether the pasta dough itself contains egg before clearing it.

wine_pairings_btg.name: The Vice Chardonnay, Napa Valley
wine_pairings_btg.note: Chardonnay's weight matches a cream-adjacent pasta and the cured yolk richness.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Paris-Simoneau Sauvignon Blanc, Val de Loire
wine_pairings_btg.note: Sauvignon keeps the asparagus and peas bright, which a heavier white would flatten.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Luli Chardonnay, Sta. Lucia Highlands, Monterey 2024
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Restrained Chardonnay that supports the pasta without burying spring vegetables.

name: Tomato Water Risotto
description: Tomato confit, garlic chip, tomato salad
tableside: Built on tomato water rather than stock, so it is clear and light rather than a deep red sauce. Tomato three ways across the plate.

dairy.note: Risotto is conventionally finished with butter and parmesan. Confirm before clearing a dairy allergy.

gluten.note: Rice based. Confirm no stock additives.

vegetarian.note: Confirm the stock base and whether parmesan is used, since parmesan uses animal rennet.

vegan.note: Depends on the butter and cheese finish. Ask the kitchen.

key_terms.definition: The clear liquid drained from crushed tomatoes, strained without pressing. Carries pure tomato flavor with no color or pulp.
The final step of risotto, beating in cold butter and cheese off the heat to make it creamy. This is where the dairy usually enters.
Cooked slowly submerged in fat at low temperature. Concentrates flavor and softens texture without browning.

chef_notes: Replaced the basil pesto risotto. Whether this can be made vegan depends entirely on the stock and the finish, so ask rather than assume a vegetable risotto is safe.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Michael-Eppan Pinot Grigio, Alto Adige
wine_pairings_btg.note: Pinot Grigio is clean and light, which suits a risotto built on clear tomato water rather than a heavy sauce.

wine_pairings_btg.name: Tement Zweigelt Rosé, Niederösterreich
wine_pairings_btg.note: Zweigelt rosé picks up the tomato acidity and adds fruit without weight.

wine_pairings_bottle.name: Terre del Barolo Arneis, Langhe 2022
wine_pairings_bottle.note: Piedmontese white with the texture for risotto and enough acidity for raw tomato salad.

name: Watermelon Salad
description: Charred cucumber, feta, cashew, mint
tableside: Cold and sharp, which makes it the best foil on the menu for anything off the rotisserie. Both the feta and the cashews are removable garnishes, so it is one of the easiest sides to modify for an allergy table.

dairy.note: Feta can be left off.

gluten.note: No gluten.

vegetarian.note: No meat or fish. Confirm feta rennet if the guest is strict.

key_terms.definition: Quick high heat applied to a vegetable normally served raw. The surface takes on smoke and softens while the centre stays crisp, which gives you two textures in one slice.

chef_notes: Both allergens here are removable garnishes, which makes this one of the easier sides to modify. Good foil for the fattier rotisserie plates.

name: Crispy Brussels Sprouts
description: Smoked blue cheese, fried shallots, honey mustard vinaigrette
tableside: Fried until the outer leaves crisp. Smoked blue cheese is assertive, so mention it to guests who are unsure about blue.

dairy.note: Blue cheese can be left off.

gluten.note: Fried shallots are often dusted in flour, and fryer sharing is a factor. Confirm before clearing a celiac guest.

eggs.note: No eggs expected. Confirm the vinaigrette.

vegetarian.note: No meat. Confirm the blue cheese rennet if the guest is strict.

key_terms.definition: Blue cheese cold smoked after aging. The smoke rounds the sharpness rather than adding to it.
Sliced thin and fried until brittle. Frequently dredged in flour or starch first, which is where the gluten risk sits.

chef_notes: Honey in the vinaigrette means this is not vegan even without the cheese. The fried shallots are the gluten question, not the sprouts themselves.

name: Buttermilk Spätzle
description: Cheese, caramelized onion
tableside: Austrian egg noodle, closer to a dumpling than a pasta. This version is essentially the Austrian answer to macaroni and cheese.

dairy.note: Buttermilk in the dough and cheese on top.

gluten.note: Wheat flour dough. Cannot be modified.

eggs.note: Egg is structural in spätzle dough. Cannot be modified.

vegetarian.note: No meat. Confirm the cheese rennet if the guest is strict.

key_terms.definition: A soft egg noodle from Southern Germany and Austria, scraped or pressed into boiling water. Irregular by nature.
The cheese and onion version, a staple across Austria and Swabia. Comparable in role to macaroni and cheese.

chef_notes: Egg and gluten are both structural in the dough and neither can be removed. This is the closest thing to a comfort food side on the menu.

name: Apricot Tart
description: Apricot kernel ice cream, cherry compote, cornbread crumble
tableside: The ice cream is made from apricot kernels, the seed inside the pit, which tastes almost exactly like almond. That is worth flagging to anyone with a nut allergy even though kernels are not technically tree nuts. Cornbread crumble ties it back to the bread service.

dairy.note: Ice cream and pastry. Central to the dish.

nuts.note: Apricot kernels are stone fruit seeds, not tree nuts, but they are chemically similar to almonds and some nut allergic guests react. Do not clear this dish on a nut allergy without the guest making an informed choice.

gluten.note: Tart shell and cornbread crumble.

eggs.note: Pastry and ice cream base commonly contain egg. Confirm.

vegetarian.note: No meat or gelatin expected. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: The seed found inside the apricot pit. It tastes strongly of almond because it contains the same aromatic compound, benzaldehyde, and it is what amaretto and much Italian pastry are built on.
Fruit cooked gently in syrup so the pieces stay whole and recognisable, rather than being broken down into a jam or a smooth puree.
The French term for stone fruit kernels used as a flavouring. The same principle behind this ice cream, and the reason a peach pit and an almond smell related.

chef_notes: The apricot kernel is the thing to communicate. It is not a tree nut in labeling terms, but it tastes like almond because it shares the same compound, and some tree nut allergic guests react to it. Give the guest the information and let them decide.

afters_pairings.name: Di9dante 'Purgatorio' Extra-Dry Vermouth
afters_pairings.why: Dry vermouth's bitter herbal edge keeps a sweet stone fruit tart from sitting heavy.

afters_pairings.name: Moscato, Di Majo Norante 'Apianae'
afters_pairings.why: Moscato's floral sweetness runs alongside apricot rather than competing with it.

name: GF Chocolate Torte
description: Spicy papaya chutney, toasted almond & coconut, chocolate passion fruit ice cream
tableside: Gluten free, but it contains almonds and coconut, so it is not the safe default for allergy tables. The chutney carries real heat.

dairy.note: Ice cream and torte.

nuts.note: Almonds and coconut. Coconut is classified as a tree nut for labeling purposes.

gluten.note: Made gluten free. Confirm prep surface separation for a celiac guest.

eggs.note: Flourless chocolate tortes are usually egg based. Confirm.

soy.note: Chocolate frequently contains soy lecithin. Confirm for a strict soy allergy.

key_terms.definition: A dense chocolate cake using ground nuts or nothing at all in place of flour. Structure comes from egg and chocolate rather than gluten.
Classified as a tree nut by the FDA for labeling even though it is botanically a drupe. Most tree nut allergic guests tolerate it, but never decide that for them.
Sharply acidic tropical fruit. The acidity is what keeps a heavy chocolate dessert from sitting flat.

chef_notes: Gluten free is not the same as allergy friendly. This dish contains almonds, coconut, dairy, and likely egg and soy. The chutney is genuinely spicy, which surprises guests on a dessert, so mention it.

afters_pairings.name: Graham's 20 Year Tawny Port
afters_pairings.why: Tawny's nuttiness and dried fruit run directly with the almond and papaya.

afters_pairings.name: Espresso Martini
afters_pairings.why: Coffee against chocolate, and the passion fruit acidity keeps it from doubling up as too rich.

name: Banana Walnut Cake
description: Buffalo Trace ice cream, cream cheese frosting, lime caramel
tableside: The ice cream is made with Buffalo Trace, so this dessert contains alcohol and should not go to a child without the parent knowing. Walnuts are baked into the cake and cannot be removed. Lime caramel is what keeps it from being too sweet.

dairy.note: Ice cream and cream cheese frosting.

nuts.note: Walnuts are baked into the cake and cannot be removed.

gluten.note: Wheat flour cake.

eggs.note: Standard in a cake batter of this type. Confirm.

soy.note: No soy expected. Confirm the caramel.

key_terms.definition: Bourbon churned into an ice cream base. Alcohol lowers the freezing point, so the scoop stays noticeably softer and melts faster than a standard ice cream.
Caramel finished with lime juice rather than cream. The acid cuts the sugar directly and stops a very sweet dessert from flattening out on the palate.

chef_notes: Contains alcohol in the ice cream, so it is not appropriate for guests avoiding alcohol or for children without the parent knowing. Walnuts are structural and cannot be removed.

afters_pairings.name: Graham's 10 Year Tawny Port
afters_pairings.why: Tawny's caramel and nut character mirrors the walnut and lime caramel without adding more sugar.

afters_pairings.name: Nonino Amaro
afters_pairings.why: Grappa-based amaro with the bitterness to cut cream cheese frosting.

name: Ice Cream Trio
description: Horchata, smores, honey butter-hazelnut
tableside: Three scoops, three flavors. The hazelnut is the one to flag for nut allergies, and the s'mores has graham in it.

dairy.note: Ice cream base.

nuts.note: Hazelnut is one of the three flavors. Ask the kitchen to substitute a different scoop.

peanuts.note: No peanuts. Confirm the s'mores components.

gluten.note: Graham cracker in the s'mores flavor. Ask for a substitute scoop.

eggs.note: Custard style ice cream bases contain egg yolk. Confirm.

vegetarian.note: Marshmallow in the s'mores flavor usually contains gelatin. Confirm.

key_terms.definition: A Latin American drink of soaked rice, cinnamon, and sugar. Traditionally nut free in the Mexican version, though the Spanish original uses tiger nuts.
Graham cracker, chocolate, and toasted marshmallow. The graham is where the gluten sits and the marshmallow is where gelatin may sit.

chef_notes: The most modifiable dessert on the menu, since individual scoops can be swapped. That makes it the right suggestion for a difficult allergy table, but confirm which substitutions are actually available that night.

afters_pairings.name: Artemisia Farms Nocino
afters_pairings.why: Walnut liqueur against the hazelnut scoop, doubling the nut character rather than contrasting it.

afters_pairings.name: Irish Coffee
afters_pairings.why: Hot and bitter against three cold sweet scoops.

name: Sorbet Trio
description: Pineapple-watermelon, blackberry-peach, kiwi-guava
tableside: Dairy free and the lightest thing on the dessert menu. This is the default recommendation for most allergy tables.

dairy.note: Sorbet is fruit and sugar based with no dairy. Confirm no shared machine concerns for a severe allergy.

gluten.note: No gluten.

eggs.note: No eggs. Confirm no egg white is used for texture.

vegan.note: Likely vegan. Confirm no honey or egg white is used.

key_terms.definition: Fruit, sugar, and water with no dairy. Distinct from sherbet, which contains a small amount of milk.

chef_notes: The safest dessert on the menu for allergy tables and the one to lead with when someone has multiple restrictions. Still worth confirming shared equipment for a severe dairy allergy.

afters_pairings.name: Moscato, Di Majo Norante 'Apianae'
afters_pairings.why: Light floral sweetness that matches sorbet without overpowering it.

afters_pairings.name: Poli Bianco Vermouth
afters_pairings.why: Aromatic and low proof, which suits a light fruit dessert better than anything spirit forward.

name: Cheese Board
description: Chef's selection of three cheeses, seasonal jam, crostini
tableside: Three cheeses, chosen by the kitchen. Ask what they are that night rather than guessing.

dairy.note: Cheese is the dish.

nuts.note: Boards of this style frequently include nuts as an accompaniment. Confirm the night's build.

gluten.note: From the crostini. Ask for a gluten free vehicle or none.

vegetarian.note: Many aged cheeses use animal rennet. Confirm the night's selection for a strict vegetarian.

key_terms.definition: An enzyme used to curdle milk. Traditionally from calf stomach, though microbial and vegetable versions exist. This is what makes some cheese non-vegetarian.
Small slices of toasted bread. The gluten vehicle on the board, separate from the cheese itself.

chef_notes: The selection changes, so confirm with the kitchen every night before describing it. Rennet is the question for strict vegetarians and it depends entirely on which cheeses are on the board.

afters_pairings.name: Doisy-Védrines Sauternes
afters_pairings.why: Botrytis sweetness against salty blue or aged cheese is the classic move.

afters_pairings.name: Graham's 20 Year Tawny Port
afters_pairings.why: Nutty and dried fruit character that works across a mixed board rather than only one style.
